For the decreasing function \(f(x)=\frac1{\sqrt{2x-1}}\),

\[
\int_k^{k+1} f(x)\,dx \le f(k) \le \int_{k-1}^k f(x)\,dx \quad (k\ge 2).
\]

Thus for \(S_n=\sum_{k=1}^n f(k)\),

\[
S_n \ge \int_1^{n+1} f(x)\,dx = \sqrt{2n+1}-1,
\]

and

\[
S_n \le 1+\int_1^n f(x)\,dx = \sqrt{2n-1}.
\]

For \(n=4901\),

\[
S_{4901} \ge \sqrt{9803}-1 > 98,
\]

since \(\sqrt{9803}>99\). Also,

\[
S_{4901} < \sqrt{9801}=99.
\]

Therefore,

\[
98 < S_{4901} < 99,
\]

so

\[
\boxed{98}.
\]
